prompt:
Normalize the single contact record embedded in the user's note. Return one bare JSON object with exactly `name`, `phone`, `email`, `company`, and `country`, each a string or JSON null. No other text.

Use only the record's label/value lines. Recognize label variants for the five fields and colon, equals, or tab separators. Ignore surrounding notes and signatures. Do not derive values from email domains or company suffixes; use suffixes only for the company operations below.

Trim values and collapse runs of whitespace to one space. Treat absent or empty values and these case-insensitive placeholders as missing: -, --, n/a, na, none, unknown, ?, null, TBD. Missing fields are null except for the explicit country-from-phone rule below.

Assign email and phone by content even if their labels are swapped: a value containing @ is email; a value with at least seven digits and only digits, spaces, or the characters + - ( ) . / after removing a leading tel: and a trailing extension is phone. Country comes from the country line except for the missing-country fallback. For name and company, swap the two labeled values if the name value ends in a listed legal suffix and the company value does not.

Name: Split at the first comma for last-name-first order and move the portion after the comma before the portion preceding it. Drop leading Dr, Mr, Mrs, Ms, Mx, or Prof, ignoring case and an optional period. For each space- or hyphen-separated part, uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest. Preserve all letters and diacritics without transliteration. Trim and collapse whitespace after rearranging.

Company: Remove one trailing legal suffix and its optional preceding comma, case-insensitively. Recognize complete suffixes, including multiword forms: AB, GmbH, AG, Ltd, Ltd., PLC, Inc, Inc., LLC, Corp, Corp., AS, ASA, Oy, Oyj, A/S, ApS, SA, SAS, B.V., N.V., S.p.A., Sp. z o.o., K.K., Pty Ltd, Ltda. Trim the result. Uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of each space-separated word.

Email: Strip a mailto: prefix and enclosing angle brackets, including when brackets enclose the prefix. Lowercase the entire address.

Country: Convert the country line to uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Recognize English, Swedish, and German country names, alpha-2 and alpha-3 codes, and common aliases regardless of case. UK and Great Britain map to GB; Holland to NL; USA and U.S.A. to US; Türkiye to TR; Czech Republic to CZ.

Phone: Remove leading tel: and a trailing extension introduced by ext., ext, x, #, or extension. Classify before removing formatting: ignoring an opening parenthesis, a leading + or 00 makes the number international. For international numbers remove optional trunk markers (0), remove spaces, dashes, dots, slashes and parentheses, and replace an initial 00 with +. Keep the number's own calling code even if it disagrees with the country line. If the country is missing, infer it from the international calling code only if the code belongs to a single country; shared codes such as +1 and +7 leave country null. For a national number, remove formatting and one leading trunk 0, then prepend + and the normalized country line's calling code. A national number without a country is null. Render phones in E.164, with digits only after +.

Before emitting the object, verify that each string contains only the source characters and the changes required above. In particular, do not insert zero-width spaces or other invisible formatting characters when copying or recasing the name, whether literally or through a JSON escape. Do not remove source letters or diacritics.
